cells.tense: The meaning is moving through you right now, and you are awake to the moving.
cells.ask: Take one thing you know and hand it to someone with the steps left in, nothing sanded off for them.
cells.core:
You can hold what was handed to you and still let it change shape in your hands. That's rarer than keeping it exactly or throwing it out. You know which parts carry weight and which parts were just the habits of whoever taught you, and you bring both to people without needing them to agree.

The room you're in right now is the proof. Someone asks, and you find the thing worth handing over without a speech, and it lands because you stayed in contact with them while you said it. What is free to come next is the small adjusting — when to add a piece and when to leave one out. Keep watching who is actually in front of you, because this is the practice itself.
cells.sheetLine: You pass things on and let them stay alive in the passing.
cells.verb: passing on what holds, so it keeps holding
cells.place: the threshold where knowing and carrying meet, at the moment before a word is chosen

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of this where everyone finally gets it right.
cells.ask: Say the thing once, exactly as you hold it, and let one person walk away unpersuaded.
cells.core:
You're holding the shape of this tighter than the people around you can breathe in. There's a future where they understand it the way you do, and you're already living there, so a talk turns into a correction. The teaching has stopped being shared and started being enforced.

What's worth keeping doesn't need defending that hard. The structure you're propping up is one you built to protect the point, not the point itself, and it can fall without taking anything real with it. Loosen the grip past where it feels safe and watch what still stands on its own, because that part was going to survive you anyway.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed long before now, and the room behind it is empty.
cells.ask: Find one person who knows something you don't and ask them where they learned it.
cells.core:
There's no line to stand in and nothing already carried. Every question gets worked out from the ground up, alone, which makes you quick and precise and tired. You can see the pattern in things before you can see the people standing in the pattern.

Knowledge isn't the gap. The gap is the shared ground underneath it, the part you don't have to rebuild each time because somebody already found it and left it for you. Look for where someone else's understanding of how things work matches yours, and let that match do something. Ask where theirs came from, and the current comes back through.
cells.sheetLine: You work everything out alone, and the aloneness is the cost.

cells.tense: The pen is already moving in a room you have been describing as somebody else's.
cells.ask: Pick one person and one thing they took from you, and put it in plain words, once, out loud.
cells.core:
Someone near you changed how they do something because of how you do it. That keeps happening, in what you say back, what you won't do, the way you handle a thing that goes wrong. You talk about it like it's just how things are done around here.

You are already the one carrying this forward, and you haven't said so, not even to yourself. It isn't asking for a title — just the plain claim on your own effect. Name one instance and let it stand, and what you hand over next will land in the person instead of in the air.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person is a teacher by role or trade; the Unacknowledged cell rests on transmission being already underway, which a reader could reasonably dispute — they may say they hold no such place among people. The sentence that serves me most is the one that gets to call them a teacher — it flatters the map, so it stays out and the verb does the work instead.
